header: Date: 2027-02-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Cruz (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (HelioHealth), Jonas Ruiz (HelioHealth CTO), Priya Mehta (HelioHealth SRE), Anil Bose (HelioHealth ML)
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review last week's throughput tests, tune autoscaling heuristics for Dedicated pools, and agree next steps for burst rehearsals. Customer wants clear fallback rules for latency-sensitive endpoints and a cost comparison for reserve vs burst capacity.
topics: Burst rehearsal plan and acceptance criteria
KV/prefix caching impact on tokens and latency
Security integration (SAML, KMS) and compliance artifacts
transcript: 00:00 Jamie Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - throughput readout, autoscale tuning, burst run scheduling. 00:12 Maya Lin: thanks jamie, brought the SRE and ML folks, we wanted to focus on the latency sensitive endpoints - the patient note summarization flow. 00:25 Evan Cruz: great, we have the 48-hour run results uploaded to the sheet, I'll pop the link in chat. quick note, we did two runs: baseline hosted variant and quantized dedicated variant with prefix caching enabled. 00:40 Jonas Ruiz: i saw the top-level numbers but i'm worried about p50 versus p95, p99 tails. last week p99 spiked to 1.8s which is above our SLA. 00:52 Evan Cruz: yeah the p99 is the stress point. we isolated some queuing around the small gpu pool when token lengths went long - the KV cash (sic) warm-up helps reduce repeated compute but the first prefix cold start still costs. 01:08 Priya Mehta: can you explain the KV cash warm up bit? we saw some warm-up spikes at 10:30 in the run. 01:16 Evan Cruz: sure, prefix cache will store the KV cache for common prefix tokens - so if your user prompt starts with the same system prompt the second request reuses KV. but when there's a new prompt pattern, you get a cold run. we recommended a short TTL and pre-warming for scheduled bursts. 01:32 Maya Lin: pre-warming sounds heavy. does that mean we need to keep capacity reserved? we have strict budget constraints. 01:39 Jamie Patel: good question. this is where reserve vs burst mix comes in. reserved capacity ensures warm caches and predictable p99 but costs more. burst lets you scale up rapidly but you accept some cold starts and slightly higher tail latencies unless you pre-warm. 01:58 Jonas Ruiz: what's Redwood's advice on cooldown and headroom settings for our traffic? our traffic doubles in morning and has random micro surges. 02:08 Evan Cruz: for the Dedicated pool we set a 25% headroom target (i.e., maintain 25% spare capacity) with a 60s scale-up cooldown and a 300s scale-down cooldown. that reduced oscillations in our tests. we also tune the batch size ceiling so small requests don't block long requests. 02:29 Priya Mehta: 25% headroom seems fair, but can we make that adaptive? like reduce headroom overnight and increase during office hours? 02:37 Evan Cruz: yes, autoscaling policies can be schedule-aware. you can define time windows with different headroom and min-replicas. we can show a JSON policy example. 02:48 Maya Lin: we'd like fallback rules as well. if dedicated capacity is saturated, can we fallback to a cheaper hosted model with degraded timeout? 02:58 Jamie Patel: absolutely — Redwood supports policy routing: prefer Dedicated, fallback to hosted small model variant or enqueue with extended timeout. you can set latency SLO thresholds to trigger fallback. 03:12 Jonas Ruiz: any impact to data residency or compliance if we fallback to hosted? 03:19 Jamie Patel: yes that is a compliance surface. fallback across environments is subject to your tenancy. for HelioHealth we can restrict fallbacks to the same region or to private VPC-compatible hosted nodes; we'll flag that in the runbook. 03:36 Anil Bose: curious about quantization tradeoffs — our classifiers lost a tiny bit of accuracy with int8 in offline evals. is Redwood seeing big delta in generation quality? 03:46 Evan Cruz: quantization can affect logit distributions slightly; for summarization we saw negligible semantic drift on our test prompts but your dataset may vary. we suggest running an eval set as part of the POC using the same prompts. 03:59 Maya Lin: ok we will annotate 200 prompts and we can compare. 04:05 Priya Mehta: regarding the 2-hour burst test — how to simulate realistic user think time and payload sizes? 04:12 Evan Cruz: use the trace we asked for - we replay request timestamps and payload sizes with jitter. also simulate conversational turns to blow up KV cache variance. 04:24 Jonas Ruiz: what acceptance criteria should we use? 04:28 Jamie Patel: propose: sustained throughput target at 95% of expected peak with p95 < 800ms and p99 < 1.6s for the primary endpoint. if we miss by more than 20% we iterate on headroom or reserve commit. 04:47 Maya Lin: fine, can you log all throttles and model fallbacks in the telemetry? we need that for incident postmortem. 04:55 Evan Cruz: yes we emit events for scale-up, scale-down, fallback, and TTL cache misses; we'll attach the event stream to the shared sheet. 05:07 Priya Mehta: about pricing - how will burst billing look? 05:12 Jamie Patel: reserved capacity is monthly commit; burst overage is billed at usage rates with tiered discounts. we'll send the spreadsheet with scenarios. 05:22 Jonas Ruiz: any competitor pitfalls we've seen? 05:26 Evan Cruz: some vendors don't support transparent fallback or per-route SLOs, or they require full reingestion for cold caches. others lock you into a single cloud region making residency hard — we flagged LargeCloudAI and OnPremCo for those patterns. 05:44 Maya Lin: security quick check - SAML, RBAC mapping, KMS for keys. can you share what Redwood needs? 05:51 Jamie Patel: yes - we'll send the SAML metadata, RBAC mapping docs, and KMS integration notes. for SOC2 cert we have a whitepaper. 05:59 Anil Bose: small note, the model variant naming in the telemetry got munged in the sheet, we had trouble mapping variant id to quantized vs fp16. 06:10 Evan Cruz: noted, we'll add a mapping column and standardize variant names. 06:16 Maya Lin: ok final recap and owners? 06:20 Jamie Patel: recap - Evan runs burst test (due Thu), Jamie sends pricing and security docs (due Wed), Maya provides traces (due Mon), Priya confirms SAML (due Fri). schedule runbook rehearsal next week. 06:36 Jonas Ruiz: thanks everyone, this helps. 06:40 Jamie Patel: thanks all, i'll follow up with invites and links. 06:45 [meeting ends]
